page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 48 GB of RAM, providing a generous 12 GB of memory per core. The host runs on the KVM hypervisor powered by AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 16 MB of L3 cache, standard hardware virtualization extensions, and cryptographic acceleration such as AES and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No local storage is bundled with this instance, requiring detached network storage volumes for stateful configurations, and no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate mixed performance characteristics shaped by the shared execution model. The instance achieves a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2,114 and an average multi-core score of 6,323, showing solid burst capability for general task execution. However, prolonged CPU loads reflect the constraints of shared AMD Zen 2 cores, with stress-ng scores settling in the lower quartiles. Memory benchmarks indicate average cached throughput (411.75 GB/s at 16 KB) but drop to weaker uncached bandwidth rates (35.68 GB/s read and 25.08 GB/s write), mirrored by a lower PassMark memory score of 1,496.72.

The primary tradeoff of the CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is its asymmetric resource distribution: substantial RAM capacity paired with shared computing resources. This makes it cost-efficient for memory-dense services that do not sustain high computational loads, such as in-memory caching layers, medium-scale Redis deployments, staging databases, staging environments, and intermediate batch processing pipelines.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 48 GB of system memory. This configuration offers an expansive 12 GB of RAM per vCPU, designed for memory-intensive applications that require moderate compute capabilities. The virtual machine runs under KVM on the x86_64 architecture with AES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware support, but includes no local storage volumes or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the server delivers strong burst single-core execution alongside mid-tier multi-threaded compile and compression performance, offset by modest sustained compute and uncached memory bandwidth metrics. Because compute resources are shared and local disks are absent, it operates as a cost-efficient deployment target for memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory datastores, caching tiers, staging databases, and memory-bound ETL services.
